feed.title: AI Tips Watch
feed.subtitle: Searchable reference of AI coding and Grok Bot tips from 16 builders on X

entry.title: Code quality: Scale human review to the stakes
entry.summary: Agent reviewers, linters and verifiers help but aren't enough; scale human review to the stakes, not to lines of code or PR counts. (Source: https://x.com/aiDotEngineer/status/2123566998294601980)

entry.title: Code quality: Slop is fine when it gets you the outcome
entry.summary: One-shot prompts and vibe coding are fine when they get you the outcome; slop is bad only when it undermines quality, maintainability or teammates' time. (Source: https://x.com/aiDotEngineer/status/2123566998294601980)

entry.title: Software factories: Warp Factories: workflows as YAML, dashboards, self-improvement
entry.summary: Define agent workflows as code in YAML; dashboards track code quality, test coverage, regression risk and cost per PR (00:51); a Self-Improvement toggle lets the loop optimize itself (00:58); built-in benchmarking compares configs, subagents and models (01:03). (Source: https://x.com/warpdotdev/status/2123493996286951624)

entry.title: Grok Bot: Give travel requests themes and dates
entry.summary: Ask for specific flights (e.g. nonstop SFO to LAX) and pick from options in chat (00:05), or give themed preferences and dates (e.g. a desert hotel near Joshua Tree) to get bookable hotel options. (Source: https://x.com/bot/status/2123121401762918718)

entry.title: Workflows: Choose the approach by change size
entry.summary: One-shot tiny changes; for big features, start with an alignment phase on domain language. (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2123098316867051991)

entry.title: Agent skills & setup: Grill first: let the agent question you before coding
entry.summary: A command like /grill-with-docs makes the agent ask you questions before it writes any code. (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2123098316867051991)

entry.title: Agent skills & setup: Keep a GLOSSARY.md of project terms
entry.summary: Agents write better code when they know your domain's nouns and verbs. (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2123098316867051991)

entry.title: Agent skills & setup: Record ADRs so agents don't undo past decisions
entry.summary: Architectural Decision Records tell the agent why past decisions were made. (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2123098316867051991)

entry.title: Workflows: Compact the planning chat into a spec and tickets
entry.summary: Before implementing, compact a long planning chat (/compact) into a clean spec and a list of tickets, then run /implement-spec. (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2123098316867051991)

entry.title: Agent skills & setup: Run /retro after a big generation
entry.summary: The agent reviews its own code against your standards for rule violations, scope creep and excess complexity. (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2123098316867051991)

entry.title: Code quality: Split a huge PR into stacked PRs
entry.summary: Have the agent break a big PR into smaller stacked PRs (e.g. schema, backend, UI) and review them one by one. (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2123098316867051991)

entry.title: Code quality: Prefer soft deletes when replacing an old system
entry.summary: Use a soft delete (e.g. an archived flag) instead of hard-deleting data, so you can revert. (No reliable timestamp in the video.) (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2123098316867051991)

entry.title: Models & evaluation: Evaluate agents on multi-step iterative tasks
entry.summary: One-shot tests miss it: watch whether agents refactor and centralize code as requirements grow, or pile on workarounds. (Source: https://x.com/i/broadcasts/2WXPoPRqBdVEPZ)

entry.title: Code quality: Watch for library avoidance
entry.summary: Agents often rewrite provided libraries from scratch instead of using them. (Source: https://x.com/i/broadcasts/2WXPoPRqBdVEPZ)

entry.title: Models & evaluation: Judge an agent-designed API by whether other agents can use it
entry.summary: LibraryDesignBench finds agent-designed libraries are often hard for other agents to use. (Source: https://x.com/i/broadcasts/2WXPoPRqBdVEPZ)

entry.title: Code quality: Python anti-patterns agents produce
entry.summary: Watch for Go-style (value, error) tuple returns in Python (21:20), catch-and-reraise at every layer instead of letting exceptions bubble up (22:20), and type(x) == T instead of isinstance() (24:25). (Source: https://x.com/i/broadcasts/2WXPoPRqBdVEPZ)

entry.title: Workflows: For big refactors, delete and reimplement from a new plan
entry.summary: Vaibhav's tip: for a big refactor or library swap, delete the old code and tests, have the agent write a new plan, and reimplement from scratch rather than editing in place. (Source: https://x.com/i/broadcasts/2WXPoPRqBdVEPZ)

entry.title: Cursor: Edit dictated prompts before sending, including follow-ups
entry.summary: Click the mic in the agent prompt box to dictate (text transcribes live); cancel or stop recording and edit before sending. It works for follow-ups too, e.g. 'Write a unit test for the dark mode toggle' (00:22). (Source: https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2122419926208249898)

entry.title: Prompting: Use a field's precise domain terms in prompts
entry.summary: Precise domain vocabulary pulls the relevant knowledge out of the model. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZBTegd8DUZM&t=455s)

entry.title: Prompting: Tell the model which trade-offs matter
entry.summary: The model's first correct solution is rarely the best one; state the trade-offs that matter for your problem. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZBTegd8DUZM&t=492s)

entry.title: Workflows: Give agents straight-line tasks toward a verifiable goal
entry.summary: Agents are strong tactically but weak at ambiguous design work that needs judgment; hand them clear tasks with a verifiable goal. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZBTegd8DUZM&t=521s)

entry.title: Code quality: Avoid nuance in the APIs and codebases agents work in
entry.summary: Ambiguity leads agents to poor choices and slop. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZBTegd8DUZM&t=548s)

entry.title: Workflows: Spend the time agents save on quality
entry.summary: Use the time saved on drudgery to raise quality, not just to ship more features. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZBTegd8DUZM&t=740s)

entry.title: Code quality: Re-check agent code's assumptions as data grows
entry.summary: Trade-offs chosen early (e.g. for an empty database) can break as data grows; revisit them over time. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZBTegd8DUZM&t=1710s)

entry.title: Prompting: Surface assumptions as editable widgets before generating
entry.summary: Feedforward UX: the AI shows its assumptions (e.g. kids' ages, interests) as editable controls before writing the plan, offers preselected style/color dropdowns for creative assets (00:26), and 'leaving blanks' templates for missing details like guest count or tone (00:41), so you steer without extra chat turns. (Source: https://x.com/liu_xingyu/status/2121015724374397183)

entry.title: Code quality: Guide agents with an inverted pyramid: deterministic first, prose last
entry.summary: Rely most on deterministic codebase design and static analysis (API design, architecture, lint rules, types, tests), then verification, and least on prose instructions (rules, skills, AGENTS.md) and human review. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=122s)

entry.title: Code quality: Turn every agent correction into a deterministic check
entry.summary: When you correct an agent, or catch something in review, make the fix a lint rule or other deterministic check in the codebase rather than new text in an instructions markdown file. Agents copy the patterns they see, so keep bad patterns out of the code. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=189s)

entry.title: Code quality: Enforce architecture with directory-based import bans
entry.summary: Encode boundaries in the directory structure and ban imports across them, e.g. code in electron-renderer can't import from electron-main. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=297s)

entry.title: Code quality: Design foolproof APIs; ban nuanced ones like useEffect
entry.summary: APIs that need nuance to use well lead to slop. Design foolproof APIs and ban nuanced ones, such as React's useEffect in product code. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=325s)

entry.title: Code quality: Stop agents writing unsolicited markdown docs
entry.summary: Agents use markdown and docs they weren't asked for to justify wrong implementations; stop them writing it. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=415s)

entry.title: Code quality: Ban imperative quick fixes like setTimeout and requestAnimationFrame
entry.summary: Quick fixes spread: in the example shown, one agent's timer hack grew to 183 timers. Ban imperative timer-based patches such as setTimeout/requestAnimationFrame. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=442s)

entry.title: Code quality: Treat code comments as liabilities
entry.summary: Comments aren't enforceable and agents use them to justify workarounds, so delete them. The team cut comments from 65,824 to 1,227 while growing to 169 lint rules. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=499s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Spend most agent tokens on verification, with an app CLI to drive the app
entry.summary: Put roughly 70% of agent token spend into verification. Give agents a CLI to drive and screenshot your app so they check their own work before human review, e.g. `app aria:click --accessible-name "Settings"`, `app snapshot`, `app screenshot proof.png`. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=601s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Model state machines with TLA+ and prove algorithms with Lean
entry.summary: Add formal verification as another layer: TLA+ to model state machines and Lean to prove algorithms. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=649s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Fuzz your UI with property-based testing (Bombadil)
entry.summary: Use property-based UI testing to fuzz the UI; the Grok Bot team uses Bombadil (github.com/antithesishq/bombadil). (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=694s)

entry.title: Agent skills & setup: Generate statecharts and other visual artifacts for reviewers
entry.summary: Have agents produce visual artifacts such as statecharts so reviewers can check behavior quickly. The statechart skill is part of pstack (github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack). (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=774s)

entry.title: Workflows: Don't automate a low-trust loop
entry.summary: If your inner agent loop produces slop, automating it just produces more. Improve constraints and self-verification first. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=948s)

entry.title: Workflows: Once the loop is high-trust, add an outer loop on triggers
entry.summary: With a trusted inner loop, add an outer loop that kicks off agents from Linear tickets, Slack messages, cron schedules, or Datadog/Sentry alerts. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_zcc6Xl12g&t=966s)

entry.title: Grok Bot: Ask the bot for things out loud during meetings
entry.summary: Once in a Zoom/Google Meet call (ask it in chat to join), the bot responds to spoken requests such as sending follow-ups, confirms with a chat reaction, and writes structured notes and action items into apps like Notion (00:18). (Source: https://x.com/bot/status/2121320089920430181)

entry.title: Grok Bot: Ask the docs for a diagram
entry.summary: On supported docs pages, 'Ask Grok Bot' answers questions about the page; asking it to walk through how Grok Bot handles a task 'with a diagram' returns a step-by-step flowchart. (Source: https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2121294195843629360)

entry.title: Agent skills & setup: How /animatic turns a PR into a narrated video
entry.summary: The agent writes a JSON storyboard, Playwright renders code frames from the PR diff, TTS reads each line and FFmpeg stitches an MP4. Voice engine (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Edge-TTS), rendering style and stitcher are CLI options (00:56); the MP4 is posted as a PR comment via the GitHub/GitLab API or saved locally (01:25). (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2121211579098083668)

entry.title: Grok Bot: Prefill links come in web and app forms
entry.summary: Shareable prefilled-prompt links work as a web link (https://cursor.com/grok-bot/link/v1/prompt?text=...) or an app link (grokbot://app/v1/prompt?text=...). (Source: https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2120959534537871653)

entry.title: Mobile & app building: Let agents check UI across device types, with a human pause
entry.summary: Expo Simulators work from local and cloud agents (00:25), let agents test UI across iPhones, Androids, foldables and watches, and the workflow can pause for a human to check the simulator before the agent ships (00:50). (Source: https://x.com/expo/status/2120924979898601506)

entry.title: Grok Bot: Pull a bot into a video call from chat
entry.summary: Invite a bot to a video call from text chat and it joins. (Source: https://x.com/bot/status/2120582957782200586)

entry.title: Grok Bot: Have bots tag each other to hand off work
entry.summary: Bots can tag one another in channels to pass work along (e.g. a research bot handing off to a copy bot). (Source: https://x.com/bot/status/2120582957782200586)

entry.title: Grok Bot: Use a bot as a safety net before sharing
entry.summary: Bots can warn you about sensitive content, e.g. confidential financials on slides, before a deck is shared externally. (Source: https://x.com/bot/status/2120582957782200586)

entry.title: Agent skills & setup: Put private skills and shared settings in the Home Repo
entry.summary: Keep private skills (sensitive workflows) and version-controlled config like settings.json in the Home Repo so the whole team gets them. (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2120847219788308872)

entry.title: Agent skills & setup: Keep custom CLI tooling in the Home Repo
entry.summary: E.g. one CLI wrapping Slack, Discord, GitHub and Google Calendar for your agents. The Home Repo can also hold an LLM wiki of markdown on audiences, business concepts and architecture (05:44). (Source: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2120847219788308872)

entry.title: Models & evaluation: Benchmark several model configs in one run on the same harness
entry.summary: Put multiple model configurations (e.g. Gemini 4 Carbon vs Gemini 4 Argon) in a single benchmark run on the same harness. (Source: https://x.com/warpdotdev/status/2120702943003574441)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Build and own a custom review agent
entry.summary: Write a review agent that enforces your own architecture, PII handling and style rules rather than relying only on off-the-shelf reviewers. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH2axUpbc&t=258s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Review in a fresh context, not self-review
entry.summary: Hand the diff to a separate reviewer sub-agent in a fresh context window. In the Warp benchmark shown, an independent reviewer averaged 71.1% correctness at $12.02 vs 68.6% at $4.82 for self-review. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH2axUpbc&t=471s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Make the reviewer return structured JSON
entry.summary: Have the reviewer output a verdict ("approved" / "needs changes" / "requires human input") plus findings with line/blocks, a suggestion and severity ("nit" / "important" / "critical"). (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH2axUpbc&t=547s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Run the agent review loop before opening the PR
entry.summary: Keep implement/review iterations inside your agent platform so GitHub isn't cluttered with bot comments. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH2axUpbc&t=710s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Cap implement/review rounds at about 3-5
entry.summary: Limit the agent implement-and-review loop to roughly 3-5 turns. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH2axUpbc&t=736s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Verify end to end in a sandbox via Chrome DevTools Protocol
entry.summary: A "Test Desktop App" skill boots the Electron app in a container (factory.yaml: os linux, arch x86_64, dockerImage warpdotdev/dev-base:latest) and drives it through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH2axUpbc&t=1230s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Have the agent record its test session as an MP4
entry.summary: Give reviewers a video of the agent's verification run. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH2axUpbc&t=1605s)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Add a merge-risk skill to every PR
entry.summary: Score the PR on Alignment, Impact, Verification, Rollback cost and Error detection, and append a low/medium/high risk rating to the PR description. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH2axUpbc&t=1715s)

entry.title: Software factories: Free course: build your own software factory (Warp Learn)
entry.summary: Warp Learn is a free, hands-on course (taught by @BHolmesDev) that goes from fundamentals to a first automation loop to a full factory with specs, risk assessment and end-to-end verification. Zach's definition: an automation loop in the cloud that orchestrates agents to build better software over time. (Source: https://x.com/zachlloydtweets/status/2123494544024973564)

entry.title: Workflows: Act as the studio exec: give agents outcomes and a budget
entry.summary: Eno made a 57-shot, 5,129-frame 3D short film with Factory's Droids (an unreleased system): his role was giving outcomes and budget while the system designed sets, props, animation, QC, sound and rendering, running Blender on a Mac mini, renting GPUs on Modal and scoring with ElevenLabs. His takeaway: future work looks like one person who knows what they want plus intelligence assembled around goals. (Source: https://x.com/EnoReyes/status/2123459510463590839)

entry.title: Testing & verification: Bombadil 0.8.0: faster browser and TUI fuzzing
entry.summary: Bombadil 0.8.0 (Antithesis's open-source browser and TUI fuzzer) is up to 4x faster for browser fuzzing and 2x for TUIs, with binary compressed traces that cut disk use and IO. Try it with chrome-headless-shell (see the Bombadil docs). (Source: https://x.com/owickstrom/status/2123389608549343504)
